points.description: Very low eigenvalue means the data has very low variance along that principal axis (eigenvector), i.e. little information/spread in that direction.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only says the component is unimportant/carries little information without mentioning low variance.

points.description: Such axes/components are not useful (redundant, correlated with other components/features) and can be discarded in dimensionality reduction.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only mentions correlation/redundancy or only discarding, but not both ideas clearly.

rubric.notes: Full marks if the student says low eigenvalues mean low variance directions and that these can be dropped/ignored in dimensionality reduction; any wording is fine. Give part marks for a vague but on-track answer (e.g. 'unimportant components'). Give none for wrong ideas such as low eigenvalues meaning high variance or being the most important components.
